target.name: Dyna Robotics
target.founder: Lindon Gao, York Yang, Jason Ma

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $120M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Dyna Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Lindon Gao, York Yang, and Jason Ma, having raised $120M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable in the robotics sector, including Series B-stage companies such as Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B), alongside earlier-stage reference points like Walden Robotics ($1.1B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. The Stage-Progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, anchoring to the $120M total raised proxy and implying a valuation of $240M. The Peer-Median method uses the median valuation across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers, yielding $1.7B, with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The disparity between methods reflects the heterogeneity of stage positioning and market timing within the peer set.

Triangulating both methods produces a range of $204M (low) to $2.0B (high) with a median of $970M. The wide band reflects meaningful uncertainty around whether Dyna's capital efficiency and stage positioning align more closely with the stage-progression anchor or with the more mature Series B peer medians. Key uncertainties include revenue traction relative to peers, burn efficiency, and whether the company's technology differentiation supports the higher end of the peer range.
